title: Work in the Age of Machines
text:
Automation is changing the job market faster than many people expected. Routine tasks in offices and factories are increasingly performed by machines and software. As a result, some workers must learn new skills to remain employed. Experts describe this process as reskilling, and many companies now pay for it.

However, not every change is negative. Machines cannot easily copy empathy, judgment, or creative thinking, so these abilities are becoming more valuable. Nurses, teachers, and designers, for example, are likely to remain in demand. Therefore, the careers of the future may depend less on memorizing facts and more on adapting to new challenges.

questions.text: According to the passage, what is happening to routine tasks in offices and factories?
options: They are being moved to other countries.
They are increasingly performed by machines and software.
They are being eliminated by governments.
They are being done only by young workers.

questions.text: According to the passage, what do machines find difficult to copy?
Why might some workers need to learn new skills?
options: Because machines are taking over some of their routine tasks.
Because their companies have closed all their offices.
Because they no longer want to work.
Because governments require an exam every year.

questions.text: What is the author's attitude toward the future of work?
options: Pessimistic, because all jobs will disappear.
Cautiously optimistic, because change also creates new opportunities.
Indifferent, because technology does not affect work.
Angry, because companies do not pay for training.

vocabulary.definition: the use of machines or software to do work that people used to do
learning a new set of skills in order to do a different job
the ability to understand and share the feelings of another person
changing your behavior to suit a new situation

paragraph_translations: Automatyzacja zmienia rynek pracy szybciej, niż wielu ludzi się spodziewało. Rutynowe zadania w biurach i fabrykach coraz częściej wykonują maszyny i oprogramowanie. W rezultacie niektórzy pracownicy muszą zdobywać nowe umiejętności, aby utrzymać zatrudnienie. Eksperci nazywają ten proces przekwalifikowaniem, a wiele firm dziś za nie płaci.

Nie każda zmiana jest jednak negatywna. Maszyny nie potrafią łatwo odtworzyć empatii, osądu ani myślenia twórczego, dlatego te zdolności stają się coraz cenniejsze. Na przykład pielęgniarki, nauczyciele i projektanci prawdopodobnie pozostaną poszukiwani. Dlatego kariery przyszłości mogą zależeć mniej od zapamiętywania faktów, a bardziej od dostosowywania się do nowych wyzwań.
